local_scope: Skimmed content/searches overview and node pages only; case existence checked with ls/grep against content/cases.
inclusion_floor: page_candidate true only for missing controlling SCOTUS, binding-in-circuit, or split-marker authority; lower-weight state/district/new-tech finds are mention-only.
source_crosscheck: Page candidates were checked against two non-CourtListener web sources where available: U.S. Reports/LOC plus Justia for SCOTUS; official circuit PDF plus a secondary web summary for circuit cases.

caption: Burdeau v. McDowell
justification: Missing controlling private-search origin case for the draft Private & Foreign Searches node: Fourth Amendment limits governmental action, not a wrongful purely private search later turned over to prosecutors without government participation.

caption: United States v. Verdugo-Urquidez
justification: Missing controlling foreign-search boundary case for the draft Private & Foreign Searches node: Fourth Amendment does not apply to search and seizure abroad by U.S. agents of a nonresident alien's foreign property.

caption: United States v. United States District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan (Keith)
justification: Missing controlling electronic-surveillance case for the draft Electronic Surveillance & Title III node: domestic-security wiretapping requires prior judicial approval; Title III national-security disclaimer was not a warrantless-surveillance grant.

caption: United States v. Giordano
justification: Missing controlling Title III suppression/authorization case: wiretap applications must be authorized by the Attorney General or specially designated Assistant Attorney General; violation of that central statutory limit requires suppression.

caption: United States v. Donovan
justification: Missing controlling Title III identification/notice case: wiretap applications must name known persons whom the government has probable cause to believe are committing the offense and whose communications it expects to intercept; important statutory-suppression boundary.

caption: Scott v. United States
justification: Missing controlling Title III minimization case: compliance with the minimization requirement is judged objectively from the agents' circumstances, not by subjective intent; needed for the draft Electronic Surveillance & Title III node.

caption: Leaders of a Beautiful Struggle v. Baltimore Police Department
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit (en banc)
justification: Missing binding-in-circuit and split-marker authority for aerial/enhanced surveillance: accessing Baltimore AIR wide-area aerial-surveillance data was a search, and warrantless operation violated the Fourth Amendment; the Carpenter/mosaic counterpoint to public-view pole-camera cases.

caption: United States v. Warshak
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
justification: Missing binding-in-circuit digital-search/third-party case: users have a reasonable expectation of privacy in stored email content held by an ISP; compelled warrantless production is a Fourth Amendment search, though good faith saved the evidence.

caption: United States v. Gratkowski
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit
justification: Missing binding-in-circuit digital third-party boundary case: no reasonable expectation of privacy in Bitcoin blockchain transactions or Coinbase records; useful adverse authority against extending Carpenter to cryptocurrency/business records.

caption: Long Lake Township v. Maxon
justification: Mention-only: real drone-surveillance frontier find, but state civil/exclusionary-rule posture and the court declined the constitutional search question, so it is below the page-candidate floor for federal searches doctrine.

caption: State v. Andrews
justification: Mention-only: real cell-site-simulator/Stingray warrant case and useful state illustration, but not SCOTUS or federal binding-in-circuit authority; below page-candidate floor.
